purpose: Exemestane is used to treat breast cancer in women who have gone through menopause. It helps lower the chance that breast cancer will come back, or it can help shrink or slow the growth of certain breast cancers. Your doctor may prescribe it after other treatments like surgery or as part of your ongoing cancer care.
how_it_works: Your body makes a small amount of estrogen even after menopause, and some breast cancers use estrogen to grow. Exemestane works by blocking an enzyme called aromatase, which your body uses to produce estrogen. By lowering estrogen levels in your body, this medicine helps starve the cancer cells so they cannot grow as easily.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes and sweating are very common. You may also notice joint or muscle aches and pains, fatigue or tiredness, headaches, trouble sleeping, nausea, and increased sweating. Some women also experience mood changes or mild depression.
warnings: This medicine can weaken your bones over time, so your doctor will likely monitor your bone density and may recommend calcium and vitamin D supplements. Do not take this medication if you have not gone through menopause, and do not take it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can seriously harm a baby. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, especially rifampin or St. John's Wort, as they can make exemestane less effective. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual bone pain, vision changes, or signs of liver problems like yellowing of the skin or eyes.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 25 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, preferably after a meal. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed one and continue your regular schedule. Never double up doses.
